evidence_snapshot.claim_scope: public repository source and release evidence only

primary_question.zh_CN: 这套工程系统如何把移动中的外部规范、稳定方法、revision-specific truth、目标实现、可执行 review、同源评测与公开 release 连接成一条可追溯而不越权的证据链？
primary_question.en: How does the system connect moving external specifications, stable guidance, revision-specific truth, target implementations, executable review, same-owner evaluation, and public release without losing provenance or authority boundaries?

audiences: repository visitors who need a one-glance front door before entering the deep atlas
PDF companion readers who need a deep Chinese-leading project map
repository readers and reusers who need a comprehensive bilingual architecture reference
maintainers who need stable IDs for later revision and figure updates

regions.owner: MCP specification maintainers, IETF/RFC authorities, and named integration providers
regions.boundary: The project can pin, interpret, and date these sources; it does not own or rewrite their normative truth.
Owns project-authored guidance, profiles, case-study records, release registers, and public evaluation artifacts; does not own target server state or external specifications.
Selects workflow and bounded references; produces analysis or patches only within the active task and target repository authority.

regions.owner: The reviewed project's application, parent process, framework, proxy, tunnel, host, and operators
regions.boundary: Canonical runtime state and side effects remain with the target system; the Field Guide repository cannot confer reachability, host acceptance, or production assurance.
Can establish the recorded installed-skill dogfood behavior and rubric outcome; cannot establish independent assurance or causal no-skill uplift.

regions.owner: Repository maintainer and Git/GitHub release workflow
regions.boundary: Publishes byte-identified repository state after bilingual, profile, package, corpus, and link validation; future source changes require a new revision decision.

nodes.responsibility: Own protocol semantics for named revisions.
nodes.authority_limit: The repository profiles are dated interpretations, not replacement normative authority.

nodes.responsibility: Own message and transport semantics used by applicable implementations.
nodes.authority_limit: HTTP controls are not applicable to parent-owned stdio merely to make a review look complete.

nodes.responsibility: Supply dated provider-specific compatibility guidance.
nodes.authority_limit: Offline or bundled guidance cannot be presented as a live compatibility check.

nodes.responsibility: Hold capability ownership, partial ordering, state/effect, egress, deployment, and verification principles whose useful life exceeds one protocol revision.
nodes.authority_limit: Stable engineering guidance does not make moving protocol facts timeless.

nodes.responsibility: Pin revision-specific MCP, JSON-RPC, HTTP, and integration reference surfaces.
nodes.authority_limit: Each profile declares source revision and assessment date; it does not collapse historical and current designs into one checklist.

nodes.responsibility: Anchor generalized method to a named small-server intervention, hardened fork, reconciliation, tests, and residual boundaries.
nodes.authority_limit: One case supplies provenance and examples, not universal proof.

nodes.responsibility: Own the release's selected guide, skill, profile, source, and publication identities.
nodes.authority_limit: It records selected identities; it does not itself prove runtime behavior.

nodes.responsibility: Register paired Chinese and English project documents and expected sync surfaces.
nodes.authority_limit: Structural pairing is not independent semantic parity measurement.

nodes.responsibility: Choose design, audit, patch-review, or spec-upgrade mode; stop proportionately when the task does not require the full workflow.
nodes.authority_limit: The skill guides agent behavior but cannot promote unknown runtime facts to verified findings.

nodes.responsibility: Supply core invariants, deployment ownership, evidence discipline, protocol selection, MCP Apps, HTTP, and mirrored revision material as selected by the controller.
nodes.authority_limit: Only the references needed for the active mode/profile should load; bundled copies remain subordinate to named source authority.

nodes.responsibility: Make claims, findings, threats, tests, upgrade retirement, receipts, bilingual coverage, links, and package structure inspectable.
nodes.authority_limit: Schema validity and link integrity are gates, not quality or security certificates.

nodes.responsibility: Fix declared revision, transport, deployment reachability, capability owner, and evidence ceiling before controls are selected.
nodes.authority_limit: Missing runtime or host evidence remains unknown rather than inferred from source layout.

nodes.responsibility: Own transport-specific parsing, framing, admission, identity, and response-delivery concerns.
nodes.authority_limit: A transport envelope must not create a more privileged copy of shared capability semantics.

nodes.responsibility: Own normalized input, semantic validation, authorization-relevant decisions, resource budgets, state transitions, effects, and result semantics shared across transports.
nodes.authority_limit: A later control cannot retroactively protect resource, state, or authority already consumed before its enforcement point.

nodes.responsibility: Own actual proxy, tunnel, host, origin, reachability, secrets, and operator policy at their respective layers.
nodes.authority_limit: Repository source cannot prove a selected host or deployed edge accepted the behavior.

nodes.responsibility: Separate model-visible, component-visible, and operator-visible projections and their authority boundaries.
nodes.authority_limit: Visibility to one consumer does not imply visibility or mutation authority for another; browser/host acceptance requires separate evidence.

nodes.responsibility: Record what source inspection, tests, function reproduction, runtime observation, named-host acceptance, or independent reproduction actually established.
nodes.authority_limit: A receipt proves only its observed boundary; projection or sanitization does not change provenance.

nodes.responsibility: Define one positive discovery canary and eight scored synthetic scenarios with isolated prompts and fixtures.
nodes.authority_limit: Synthetic coverage is selected judgment coverage, not a statistical sample of production deployments.

nodes.responsibility: Execute the installed skill against each isolated scenario and capture process/turn/tool evidence.
nodes.authority_limit: Runtime-reported model identity is unknown; execution is same-owner.

nodes.responsibility: Distinguish process exit, thread/turn completion, trace completeness, final-message availability, skill loading, and oracle access evidence.
nodes.authority_limit: Observer blind spots create evaluator defects, not retroactive skill failures.

nodes.responsibility: Publish complete final answers and schema-v2 same-owner receipts while keeping private raw JSONL and tool traces outside the repository.
nodes.authority_limit: Public projection preserves declared provenance and cannot transform same-owner evidence into independent evidence.

nodes.responsibility: Admit only valid-completed runs, assess critical items, and bind each result to the rubric/scenario revision used for that run.
nodes.authority_limit: Old output is not re-scored under a new rubric; same-owner adjudication is not independent measurement.

nodes.responsibility: Route observer defects to the observer, language-control defects to prompts/scenario revisions, and rubric defects to a new rubric followed by reruns.
nodes.authority_limit: Evaluator repair must not silently modify the skill bytes being evaluated.

nodes.responsibility: Check tests, syntax, version register, profile mirrors, bilingual coverage, skill package, links, review bundle, and evaluation corpus.
nodes.authority_limit: Passing repository gates proves the named artifacts and checks, not deployed behavior or independent assurance.

nodes.name_zh_CN: Git commit, tag, and release object
nodes.name_en: Git commit, tag, and release object
nodes.responsibility: Identify and publish the exact public repository state selected for release.
nodes.authority_limit: Release identity does not erase declared evidence limitations or create stranger adoption evidence.

nodes.responsibility: Detect a new specification, integration change, field case, or evaluation failure and route it to the correct artifact owner.
mechanism_or_state: stable-core change only when principle changes
nodes.authority_limit: A new source does not authorize silently rewriting historical profiles or old evidence.

unknowns_and_non_claims.statement: The runtime did not report a model identity more specific than the requested gpt-5.6-sol label.
Release 2.0.1 does not establish independent assurance.
No causal no-skill A/B comparison was performed.
Public evidence does not yet establish how unfamiliar independent maintainers will use, modify, or operationalize the repository.
Target runtime, proxy, tunnel, browser, and named-host behavior remain unknown until the corresponding boundary is actually observed.

views.title_zh_CN: 先认清谁拥有真相，才决定该加什么 control
views.title_en: Name the authority before prescribing the control
views.purpose: Give repository visitors a one-glance review route from named authority through method/profile selection and target ownership to a bounded decision, while keeping target runtime truth outside repository authority.
views.renderer_guidance: Use one wide editorial spread with four line-led judgment stages and a separate target-authority band. Preserve the N/R/S/U coordinates in visible copy, keep U4 explicit, and show that only the target-authorized path owns runtime truth. Chinese and English are native language siblings of the same geometry; this summary view does not replace or crop the deeper V-REVIEW atlas.

views.title_zh_CN: Authority · Artifact · Execution · Evidence · Evaluation · Release
views.title_en: Authority · Artifact · Execution · Evidence · Evaluation · Release
views.purpose: Comprehensive cross-plane repository architecture for the public project and the attachment's navigational overview.
views.renderer_guidance: For portrait publication, stack R0-R5 as horizontal owner bands, keep the main truth route top-to-bottom, and route evaluation/maintenance returns through side gutters. For repository or full-screen inspection, place R0-R5 as left-to-right owner planes and preserve the complete cross-plane and return topology. Both layouts remain native geometry siblings of this semantic view; neither is a crop, rotation, or separate semantic authority.

views.title_zh_CN: 一次 review 怎样穿过 ownership 与 enforcement boundaries
views.title_en: How one review crosses ownership and enforcement boundaries
views.purpose: Show preflight, selected references, transport envelopes, shared capability core, deployment owners, evidence receipts, and applicability/unknown decisions.
views.renderer_guidance: The portrait sibling uses one vertical route from named authority through target preflight, selected references, transport admission, the shared capability core, deployment/projection owners, receipts, and the decision rail. The landscape sibling uses wide authority, routing, and execution bands so enforcement order and peer owners can be inspected side by side. Preserve the later-control-cannot-protect-earlier-consumption constraint in both.

views.title_zh_CN: Evaluation 如何发现并修正自己的测量缺陷
views.title_en: How evaluation detects and repairs its own measurement defects
views.purpose: Show corpus, installed runs, observer, public projections, frozen rubric, defect routing, reruns, results, and release without implying skill-byte changes or independent assurance.
views.renderer_guidance: The portrait sibling uses a forward execution/evidence spine plus explicit side-gutter repair loops to scenario/prompt, observer, and rubric. The landscape sibling uses left-to-right skill, evaluation, and release owners with the repair boundary occupying its own wide lower band. Both show rerun returning to installed execution while skill bytes remain fixed.

layout_variants.reader_job: Continuous PDF, print, and narrow-document reading
layout_variants.contract: Native portrait geometry with one dominant vertical reading direction; never a crop, rotation, or splice of the landscape scene.

layout_variants.reader_job: Repository exploration, desktop inspection, and wide-screen architecture discussion
layout_variants.contract: Native landscape geometry preserving the same selected view, stable IDs, edge meanings, versions, states, evidence status, and unknowns as its portrait sibling.

layout_variants.reader_job: One-glance README orientation before entering the deep architecture atlas
layout_variants.contract: Native 16:9 editorial geometry with Chinese and English language siblings. It is a separately selected summary view, not a crop, splice, or replacement for V-REVIEW.

render_contract.semantic_rule: A renderer may change coordinates or shorten visible node copy, but it may not delete a required node, region, state owner, feedback edge, version boundary, evidence status, or unknown from the selected view. Each selected view follows its declared layout variants: the deep atlas preserves native portrait and landscape siblings, while V-FRONT declares one wide repository-front-door geometry with native Chinese and English language siblings. No variant is a crop, rotation, splice, or independent semantic truth. A materially different question still requires a separately selected view.
render_contract.typography: Serif/Song-led semantic labels and prose; mono for stable IDs, revisions, evidence states, and receipts; no large bold Hei/sans technical shorthand.
render_contract.visual_language: White field, fine rules, nested planes, deliberate routing gutters, stable coordinate IDs, restrained dawn blue/verified green/ochre/carmine status accents, no default Mermaid theme and no sterilized six-node flow.
render_contract.shared_ids: All PDF and repository views retain the N/R/S/E/U identifiers in editable source or legend so details remain cross-addressable.
